subject: Modular packaging pathways — seat vs throughput tradeoffs
messages:
From: Ellie Barnes <ellie@clearpoint.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Gabe Torres <gabe.torres@clearpoint.ai>, ClearPoint Procurement <procurement@clearpoint.ai>
Date: Sat, 18 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging ask — seat vs throughput options and downgrade flexibility

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking this. We pulled together our usage patterns and the procurement team flagged the need to understand: 1) recommended packaging for our mix of latency-sensitive inference and bulk embedding jobs, 2) downgrade/swap rules if we shift more to throughput mid-term, and 3) what feature bundles are mandatory vs optional for our use case.

I've attached a short doc that summarizes our monthly token mix and peak windows (clearpoint_request.pdf). Can you and your team propose 2–3 concrete package options (recommended, conservative, low-cost) and indicate upgrade/downgrade implications?

We'd like to review this with your side next week. Availability: Tue/Wed afternoons PST.

Best,
Ellie
Product & ML Ops
ClearPoint AI

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging ask — seat vs throughput options and downgrade flexibility

Hi Ellie — thanks for the summary and the doc. Team, bringing you in to align on options before the call.

Ellie — high level thoughts (we'll put these in a short one-pager and a spreadsheet ahead of the workshop):

- Recommended (balanced): Dedicated mid-tier seats + burst throughput pool. Good for mixed latency + periodic bulk embedding. Preserves predictable latency during spikes.
- Conservative (latency-first): Larger dedicated seat count, smaller shared throughput. Best if you cannot tolerate token-level variability. Higher fixed commit.
- Low-cost (throughput-first): Metered throughput plan with quantization recommendations and intelligent caching. Lowest committed cost but requires more fallbacks for latency-critical endpoints.

Key upgrade/downgrade rules we propose:
- Upsize: immediate (scale seats or add throughput buckets) with prorated charge for remainder of billing cycle.
- Downsize: allowed at quarter boundaries with 30 days notice; rolling down more than 30% requires 60-day notice for elasticity safety.
- Feature swaps (e.g., removing real-time routing or reducing priority burst): supported at any time, no contract amendment for toggling optional add-ons.

I'll attach the draft scenarios and an anchor pricing table so procurement has a view. Can we lock a 45-min slot on Tue 21 Sep 2027 1:30pm PST? If not, Wed 22 Sep 2pm PST also works.

Next steps: we'll produce a short decision matrix and a bulleted SOW-style note outlining the downgrade guardrails (so procurement has contractual language).

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Packaging ask — seat vs throughput options and downgrade flexibility

Marissa — thanks, that summary is helpful. A couple quick clarifications before the workshop:

1) For the low-cost throughput-first option, what are realistic latency ranges for inference endpoints (p95) if we rely on intelligent caching + quantization?
2) On downgrade timing: our procurement lead wants a clear example of how a 40% reduction would be handled in month terms (e.g., what bills look like Q1 vs Q2).
3) Is there a pilot/short-term evaluation you can offer that lets us test burst behavior without a 12-month commit?

Procurement note: they're open to a 12-month with better anchoring, but would like an achievable mid-commit exit path if workload drops materially.

See you Tue 21 Sep 2027 13:30 PST — bringing Gabe and procurement.

Best,
Ellie

Hi Ellie / Gabe / Procurement team — Ben here (solutions & pricing). Quick answers and a concrete anchor so procurement can evaluate: 

1) Latency (low-cost plan with aggressive quantization + caching): typical p95 for short-text generation endpoints ~220–360ms; for long-context (>2k tokens) p95 increases to ~480–900ms depending on model variant. We'll include model-specific profiles in the one-pager.

2) Downgrade example (40% reduction):
- Quarter 1 (commit active): billed at committed rate for seats + consumed throughput.
- At quarter boundary, if you elect to drop 40%, you'd receive a prorated credit for the unused portion of throughput buckets and a 45-day reconfiguration window before seat reductions take effect. Net effect: first month post-change still shows partial invoice for reserved capacity to cover reconfiguration risk. We can include exact numbers in the spreadsheet.

3) Pilot: yes — 60-day pilot on a metered throughput agreement with a capped burst allowance. If you convert to a 12-month commit within the pilot, we can apply pilot usage toward commit for a 15% credit.

Commercial anchor (example):
- 12mo commit, balanced pack: base $85k/mo committed; includes up to 3 dedicated seats and 1TB/month embedding throughput; overages billed at tiered rates.
- Pilot option: month-to-month throughput cap $28k/mo plus capped burst at predefined cost multiplier.

We can offer a 15% one-time discount off list pricing in exchange for a 12-month commit with a standard downgrade guardrail (quarter-boundary changes, 30–60 day notice depending on magnitude).

Next steps: I'll drop the finalized spreadsheet into the shared doc and push a short SOW snippet for procurement review. If the commercial anchor looks reasonable we'll prepare a DocuSign with CP-2027-093 as the reference.

Ben Carter

Redwood Inference
